notes:
Statistics retained as printed. Original and replication tests extracted independently. No metric conversion. Original outcome is recall of individual items; replication describes its results tables as correctly recalled lists while methods concern word order. Corresponding main effect matched by experiment and factor; this outcome-label discrepancy is retained. Narrative affirms an irrelevant-speech effect but gives no explicit replication-success verdict for that effect; reported_success left null.
Completion source review (n_r): Procedure explicitly divides participants into two groups of 14, each completing both task conditions used in the main-effect analysis.
Completion source review (es_value_r): Named Experiment 3 main effect; preserve printed partial eta-squared without metric conversion.
Completion source review (pval_value_r): Exact p printed for the same main-effect F test and partial eta-squared.
Completion source review (reported_success): Authors state that a main effect of irrelevant speech is observed; the noninterpretability discussion concerns testing independence when the separate word-length effect is absent.
Completion source review (n_o): Explicit experiment-specific 24 participants, full design allocation and participant-level ANOVA establish the model sample; not a whole-paper recruitment count and not inferred from df. No arithmetic-derived N.

Completion source review (pval_value_o): Printed p < .001 belongs to the same named main-effect F test; bound and printed precision preserved.
